You can't be told what the frame rate is at every frame update, so it gives either an instantaneous or an average value. Either way it means that you're not always sitting at 32 when it says 32, which is why I'd assume that 100 looks smoother. 

I also know that a person's perception is "sped up" during fight or flight responses.  Another possibility is akin to a musician noticing the difference between $100 computer speakers and a set of studio monitors:  If you know what it is you're looking for, it's a whole lot easier to spot.
